rows.what the ink shows: The cancelled run retains an initial pair of uprights and several low joined strokes, but the horizontal cancellation and weak ink obscure the bodies of the proposed words. All three words cannot be verified separately.

The right-hand continuation has several low connected strokes, a deeper angular turn, and a long terminal run. The interior letters and the proposed hyphen are not separately resolved well enough to assert the full word.

A descending initial p and a low rounded following group survive the strike. The central and final letters are merged with the heavy horizontal stroke, so the apparent absence of a separate q descender does not securely distinguish pourvu from puisque.

Several short joined forms and a dense overwritten group precede the separate cancelled dans. The deletion layer cannot be cleanly allocated against the retained des and x_i, so the complete deleted des remains uncertain.

The cancelled word has a tall initial d-like stroke and a hooked terminal stroke; the low middle is almost entirely absorbed by the cancellation. Those surviving ends do not independently establish the full dans body.

The separate E has upper, middle and lower rightward strokes and a single lowered 1 to its right. To its left, the dense cancelled Lambda and small remnants do not isolate a membership sign, so the relation remains uncertain while E_1 is readable.

A tall stroke and a following low run lie in the crossed and closely joined material beside toutes les. The supposed deleted l and e cannot both be separated securely from the adjacent retained letters.

The lower cancelled word has an initial c-like curve, a loop dropping below the line, and a later tall stroke. The long heavy bar covers the intervening letters, so these fragments do not establish the complete composantes word; the clearer inserted words above belong to another layer.

At the right end of the cancelled clause a dot and final upright with a short foot remain visible. The preceding s/o body is hidden in the horizontal strike, so the visible i/t ending alone does not establish soit.

The small superscript has a loop to the right of a thicker left stem, whose lower tip projects below the loop; this favors p over a single closed 0. The separately inspected p in the upper displayed formula has the same loop-and-stem construction, with a longer stem.

The lower-right index is a short, thick oblique stroke with a rounded upper end. No detached dot is securely distinguishable from the surrounding speckle, and the stroke lacks the clear head-and-stem structure of the upper formula’s 1; the two candidates remain unresolved.
Two heavy crossing strokes cover the initial and medial bodies. A final downward stroke with a leftward lower hook remains compatible with f, but it does not establish the preceding s-a-u sequence.
The initial capital has an upright and a rounded loop closing against it, supporting D. The following low trace coincides with the thick deletion bar, so an independent e body cannot be recovered.

A detached dot and short initial upright precede the low n and open v, followed by an angular a, low r, another dotted i, and the final low e. This ordered i-n-v-a-r-i-e sequence distinguishes invarie from conserve.
An initial curved hook and a tall terminal stroke protrude above the thick cancellation. The medial body is absorbed into that bar, so the complete c-e-t sequence cannot be confirmed.

The cancelled cluster retains a left loop, a central descending stroke, and a final taller stroke with a low rightward foot. Their ordered letter bodies are obscured by the diagonal deletion; neither esp nor the possible competing cet is established.

Two separated cancelled groups lie below the inserted conditions. Only isolated humps and uprights project from their heavy horizontal bars; neither complete word body can be read, so the original two-word illegibility is retained.

The first letter has a closed low bowl and a tall right ascender, forming d. A small attached low hump and terminal rightward trace provide the compressed e; there is no initial e followed by an independent crossed t.

The formula has a short curved n above the triangular Lambda and a separate low cup-shaped u at its right. The cancellation crosses the prose baseline; several upper humps and a final raised accent survive, but they do not establish the full bodies of se ramène.
An initial short upright and dot survive, with two later tall crossing strokes. The long thick cancellation covers the intervening letter bodies, so si est de is not fully recoverable.
Beneath the short cancellation, the left letter retains an open curved c and the right letter a small closed lower e loop.

Below the separate inserted tous, a dark initial loop and several short upper strokes remain under the deletion. The thick baseline and final overstroke conceal enough of the middle and ending that the full word prenant cannot be verified.

The inserted de n stands above the cancellation. At the deleted baseline only a short initial rise and a tall descending terminal stroke remain distinct; the connected bodies needed for au are hidden.
Immediately after indices there is one word: a looped d, dotted i, short s, tall t, second dotted i, low n, and crowded c-t-s ending. There is no intervening separate deux à deux sequence.

A separate heavy mark follows triangulaire: it has a hooked upper cap and a descending diagonal taper. No detached point is clearly established beneath it, and the curved shape does not securely distinguish the proposed question mark from a slash.

Before the closing parenthesis the compressed group begins with a low open loop and long connector, has a small raised mark, and ends in two dark short clusters. The individual bodies do not securely yield either full candidate; an accent and terminal abbreviation point for supér. are not independently clear.
